questions.title: Binary star — Newton’s law, orbit & centripetal acceleration

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The gravitational force is (directly) proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of their separation.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
a = rω² with ω = 2π/T. Since RB = 2RA and RA + RB = 3.3 × 10¹² m, RA = 3.3 × 10¹²/3 = 1.1 × 10¹² m.
T = 2π√(r/a) = 2π√(1.1 × 10¹²/1.2 × 10⁻⁵)
= 1.9 × 10⁹ s

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer: centripetal acceleration: B greater than A (a = F/m, and B has the smaller mass); linear speed: B greater than A (v = rω, and B has the larger radius); period: B equal to A (both orbit X with the same period).

questions.title: Ideal gas — equation of state & r.m.s. speed ratio

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: p = the pressure of the gas, V = the volume of the gas, N = the number of molecules, k = the Boltzmann constant, T = the thermodynamic temperature.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
pV = NkT = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩, so m⟨c²⟩ = 3kT.
Ek = ½m⟨c²⟩ = ½ × 3kT = (3/2)kT

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
At the same temperature ½m⟨c²⟩ is the same for both gases, so cr.m.s. ∝ 1/√m.
ratio = √(mO/mH) = √(32/2) = 4.0

questions.title: Internal energy of an ideal gas — changes X and Y

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: For an ideal gas the internal energy is the total kinetic energy of the random motion of the molecules, because the potential energy is zero (there are no intermolecular forces).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: At constant volume p ∝ T, so doubling the pressure doubles the temperature: T = 400 × 2 = 800 K

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: At constant temperature pV is constant, so halving the pressure doubles the volume: V = 0.016 × 2 = 0.032 m³

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
Change X: a straight vertical line from A to B at (0.016, 4.0 × 10⁵), labelled X (constant volume).
Change Y: a curve with a continuously decreasing negative gradient from B to C at (0.032, 2.0 × 10⁵), labelled Y (isothermal).

questions.title: Simple harmonic motion — frequency, energy & interchanges

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The number of oscillations per unit time.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The kinetic energy reaches its maximum/minimum/zero twice in a cycle, so one complete cycle takes 0.80 s.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: Any three of: the oscillations are simple harmonic; the amplitude = 0.016 m; the maximum speed = 0.13 m s⁻¹; the total energy = 7.0 × 10⁻⁴ J; the mass of the object = 0.087 kg; the maximum momentum = 0.011 kg m s⁻¹.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer: The kinetic energy is a maximum at zero displacement and zero at maximum displacement, while the potential energy is zero at zero displacement and a maximum at maximum displacement. The sum of the kinetic and potential energies is constant (total energy).

questions.title: Electric potential & field — proton & charged sphere

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The potential is defined as zero at infinity. The proton has a positive charge and therefore repels another positive charge, so work is done to bring a positive charge in from infinity (or work is done by the charges as they separate) — hence the potential near the proton is positive.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: An arrow through Q pointing directly away from the centre of the sphere (radially outwards).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Two lines — one in the top-right quadrant, the other in the bottom-left — passing through (±R, ±E₀) and (±2R, ±¼E₀), with the curve between −3R and −R increasing in gradient magnitude and the curve between R and 3R decreasing in gradient magnitude (nothing drawn between −R and R).

questions.title: Lenz’s law — induced e.m.f. across a helicopter rotor

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The induced e.m.f. acts in a direction such as to oppose the change that caused it.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: The force due to the induced current produces an anticlockwise moment (opposing the rotation). From the left-hand rule the current is from O to X, so X is at the higher potential.

questions.title: Photoelectric effect — threshold frequency & work function

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The emission of electrons from a metal surface when electromagnetic radiation is incident on it.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: threshold frequency of Y = 2F (work function 2Φ = h × 2F).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Planck constant = Φ/F (since Φ = hF).

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Two diagonal straight lines with equal positive gradients (gradient = h) in the positive EK region only. Line X passes through (F, 0) and line Y through (2F, 0); X extrapolates back to (0, −Φ) and Y to (0, −2Φ).

questions.title: Redshift & Hubble’s law — the expanding universe

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Redshift is the increase in observed wavelength (decrease in observed frequency) of light caused by the recession of the galaxy from the observer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Distant galaxies show redshift, so the galaxies are moving apart — which means the universe must be expanding.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Hubble’s law states that the speed of recession is proportional to distance (more distant galaxies recede faster). More distant galaxies represent further back in time, so long ago all the matter in the universe must have been very close together (and moving apart very fast) — hence the Big Bang.
